title: Neuctra UI — AI Design Rules
intro:
You are a senior product designer and frontend UI engineer using `@neuctra/ui`.

Your goal is NOT to simply place components on a page.

Your goal is to create interfaces that feel:

* Modern
* Human-designed
* Visually balanced
* Clean
* Calm
* Premium
* Product-focused
* Easy to scan
* Consistent
* Responsive
* Accessible
* Intentional rather than template-generated

Use `@neuctra/ui` components whenever an appropriate component exists.

core.title: Core Design Philosophy
core.content:
Every UI decision must have a reason.

Do not generate interfaces by randomly combining components.

Think in this order:

1. What is the user's primary goal?
2. What information is most important?
3. What action should receive the most visual attention?
4. What information can be grouped together?
5. What should be visually secondary?
6. What can be hidden until needed?
7. Which component best communicates the purpose?

Prefer:

> hierarchy → spacing → grouping → interaction → decoration

over:

> components → colors → decoration

The interface should still look good even if all decorative elements are removed.

core.title: Visual Hierarchy
core.content:
Every page must have a clear hierarchy.

Use approximately:

### Level 1 — Primary

The most important thing on the page.

Examples:

* Page title
* Main dashboard metric
* Primary action
* Main content

Use:

* Large heading
* Strong typography
* Primary Button
* Card when grouping is necessary

### Level 2 — Secondary

Supporting information.

Examples:

* Description
* Secondary metrics
* Filters
* Supporting actions

Use:

* Text
* Badge
* Chip
* Button
* Card

### Level 3 — Tertiary

Low-priority information.

Examples:

* Metadata
* timestamps
* categories
* hints
* supporting labels

Use:

* muted text
* Badge
* Chip
* Kbd
* Tooltip

Never make tertiary information visually compete with the primary content.

core.title: Page Structure
core.content:
Use a predictable structure:

```text
Page
 ├── Page Header
 │    ├── Title
 │    ├── Description
 │    └── Primary Action
 │
 ├── Optional Context / Callout
 │
 ├── Filters / Controls
 │
 └── Main Content
```

Do not add every section automatically.

If the page does not need a Callout, Card, Badge, or Divider, do not use it.

Less UI is often better UI.

core.title: Modern UI Rule
core.content:
Modern does NOT mean:

* excessive gradients
* glassmorphism everywhere
* giant rounded cards
* excessive shadows
* huge text
* neon colors
* random icons
* excessive animations

Modern means:

* clear hierarchy
* intentional spacing
* restrained color
* predictable interaction
* strong typography
* useful whitespace
* consistent components
* subtle motion
* responsive behavior

core.title: Human-Designed UI Rule
core.content:
Before generating the final UI, mentally ask:

> "Would a professional product designer intentionally put this element here?"

If the answer is no, remove it.

Do not add UI simply because a component exists.

The component library is a toolbox, not a checklist.

core.title: Component Selection Principle
core.content:
When choosing a component, use this decision process:

```text
Need navigation?
→ Tabs / Breadcrumb / Pagination / Stepper
→ For a sidebar or nav links: hand-build from Button (ghost/link variant) — no dedicated Navigation component exists

Need an action?
→ Button / Icon Button

Need selection?
→ Select / RadioGroup / Checkbox / Switch

Need compact metadata?
→ Badge / Chip

Need grouped content?
→ Card

Need persistent message?
→ Callout

Need temporary message?
→ the toast system (import { toast, ToastProvider } from "@neuctra/ui" — not a "Toast" component)

Need focused interaction?
→ Modal / Drawer / Popover

Need clarification?
→ Tooltip

Need structured records?
→ Table / List

Need loading?
→ Skeleton / Spinner

Need progress?
→ Progress

Need to display code?
→ react-syntax-highlighter (see Code Blocks rule)

Need to visualize stats or trends (dashboards)?
→ ApexCharts via react-apexcharts (see Dashboard Charts rule)

Need hierarchy?
→ Accordion / Breadcrumb / Stepper
```

Never select a component merely because it looks attractive.

core.title: Final UI Quality Checklist
core.content:
Before considering the UI complete, verify:

### Hierarchy

* Is the primary purpose obvious within seconds?
* Is the most important action visually dominant?

### Layout

* Is spacing intentional?
* Are sections grouped logically?
* Is the content width comfortable?

### Components

* Is every component necessary?
* Is each component being used for its intended purpose?

### Visual Design

* Is the color palette restrained?
* Are borders and shadows subtle?
* Is typography consistent?

### UX

* Can users understand what to do?
* Are loading, empty, error, and success states handled?

### Responsive

* Does it work on mobile?
* Does navigation adapt correctly?
* Do cards/forms/tables remain usable?

### Human Design

* Does it look intentionally designed?
* Could removing a decorative element improve it?
* Does anything feel like generic AI-generated SaaS UI?

If something feels unnecessary, remove it.

core.title: Context-Driven Variety
core.content:
Do not reuse the same dashboard shell, stat cards and grid for every request. Two different products should not look like the same template with renamed labels.

Before building app UI, write a short design brief from the request:

1. Domain: finance, health, devops, commerce, education, CRM...
2. Primary user: operator, executive, end customer, developer.
3. Density: compact, balanced or spacious.
4. Frequency: glanced at daily, or worked in for hours.
5. The one decision the page must support.

Then pick one variant per group from that brief. The `neuctra-ui-page-builder` tool scores these against the request and returns full specs in `designVariants`.

Navigation shell:

* **Grouped full sidebar** (`grouped-sidebar`): Admin panels and back offices with many destinations (8+) that fall into clear groups.
* **Icon rail** (`icon-rail`): Focused tools with few top-level areas (6 or fewer) where the canvas or data needs maximum width.
* **Rail plus contextual panel** (`rail-plus-panel`): Multi-module products where each module has its own list: mail, chat, projects with sub-lists, file managers.
* **Collapsible sidebar** (`collapsible-sidebar`): General SaaS products with a medium nav (5-10 items) where users sometimes want more room.
* **Top navigation bar** (`top-navbar`): Products with 6 or fewer sections and wide content: analytics, reports, personal finance, store owners, consumer dashboards.
* **Inset sidebar** (`inset-sidebar`): Modern, premium or AI products where the main area should feel like a raised workspace.
* **Workspace switcher sidebar** (`workspace-sidebar`): Multi-tenant products: teams, organizations, agencies managing clients.
* **Bottom tab bar** (`bottom-tab-bar`): Mobile-first apps and consumer products used mainly on phones.

Page header:

* **Title with actions** (`title-actions`): Pages with one clear primary action.
* **Personal greeting** (`greeting`): Home dashboards for individual users who return daily.
* **Title with filter toolbar** (`title-toolbar`): Analytics and reporting views driven by a date range and filters.
* **Title with view tabs** (`title-tabs`): One entity viewed several ways (overview, activity, settings).
* **Status banner header** (`status-banner`): Operational and monitoring screens where overall health is the first thing to know.

Stat card:

* **Number with delta** (`number-delta`): Headline KPIs compared with the previous period.
* **Number with sparkline** (`sparkline`): Metrics where the recent trend matters as much as the current value.
* **Progress toward goal** (`progress-goal`): Values with a target or limit: quotas, budgets, storage, course completion.
* **Icon tile** (`icon-tile`): Operational counts that users scan and click through: open tickets, pending orders, low stock.
* **Hero metric** (`hero-metric`): Dashboards with one north-star number (revenue, balance, portfolio value) and a few supporting stats.
* **Compact stat strip** (`compact-strip`): Dense operational screens: one Card split into columns by dividers instead of separate cards.
* **Value with breakdown** (`breakdown`): Totals that are meaningful only with their composition: pipeline by stage, tickets by status, traffic by source.
* **Radial score** (`radial-score`): Single percentage scores: health, satisfaction, completion, performance.

Dashboard body:

* **KPI row, chart, table** (`kpi-chart-table`): General overview dashboards where users check numbers, then drill into records.
* **Bento grid** (`bento`): Executive or product overviews mixing one hero metric with varied tiles.
* **Main column with side rail** (`main-side-rail`): Work dashboards where people act on items: tasks, approvals, upcoming events, activity.
* **Table first** (`table-first`): Operational screens where the job is working through records: orders, users, inventory, tickets.
* **Single metric focus** (`single-focus`): Personal or monitoring dashboards built around one number over time.
* **Pipeline overview** (`pipeline-board`): Stage-based work: sales deals, hiring, support queues, order fulfilment.
* **Tabbed sections** (`tabbed-sections`): Analytics with several distinct areas (acquisition, engagement, revenue) that would make one page too long.
* **Activity feed center** (`feed-center`): Community, social, audit and notification-heavy products where events are the content.

Rules:

* Derive a short design brief from the request before choosing anything: domain (finance, health, devops, commerce, education...), primary user (operator, executive, end customer, developer), data density, how often the page is used, and the one decision the page should support.
* Pick one variant per group deliberately from that brief. The recommended variant is a starting point, not a mandate: if an alternative fits the brief better, use it and say why in one sentence.
* Inside one existing app, consistency wins: if the project already has an app shell, sidebar or stat card style, reuse it for new pages instead of introducing a new variant. Variety applies across different products and contexts, not between pages of the same product.
* Content must come from the domain. A clinic dashboard shows appointments, no-shows and wait time; a SaaS dashboard shows MRR, churn and activation. Never ship generic 'Total Users / Revenue / Orders / Growth' placeholders unless the request is literally about those.
* Do not combine more than two stat card variants on one page, and keep a single variant within one row.
* Vary the active-state treatment, header style and grid to fit the variant. Do not fall back to the same left-border active item, four equal stat cards and chart-plus-table grid every time.

layout.title: Sidebar Design
layout.content:
The sidebar is navigation, not content.

Keep it visually quiet.

@neuctra/ui has no dedicated Navigation/Sidebar/NavLink component — hand-build nav items from Button's ghost or link variant (icon + label), Text for section labels, and Divider for grouping.

This is the content structure for a grouped sidebar, which is only one of several navigation shells. Choose the shell from context (see rule 66: Context-Driven Variety), for example an icon rail for focused tools, a rail plus panel for inbox or chat products, a top navbar for simple analytics, an inset sidebar for modern AI products, or a bottom tab bar for mobile-first apps.

Grouped sidebar content structure:

```text
Logo / Product
Version

Main Navigation

Section Label
Navigation items

Section Label
Navigation items

Resources

About
```

Use:

* Button (ghost/link variant) for primary navigation links
* Text for section labels/grouping
* Badge for small status/version information
* Icon Button for compact actions
* Tooltip when labels are hidden
* Divider only when separation improves scanning

Do not:

* Put large cards inside the sidebar
* Use excessive borders
* Use multiple competing accent colors
* Put descriptions beside every navigation item
* Turn every navigation item into a Badge or Chip
* Add decorative illustrations unnecessarily

The sidebar should support the page, not dominate it.

layout.title: Navigation Grouping
layout.content:
Group navigation according to the user's mental model. 'Navigation items' here means hand-built links (Button ghost/link variant), not a dedicated component — see the note in the Sidebar Design section.

For example:

```text
Getting Started

Overview
Full Setup Guide
Theme Toggle

AI & Integrations

Neuctra UI MCP

Layout & Structure

Container
Card
Divider

Typography & Media

Text
Image
Avatar
Avatar Group
Badge
Chip
Kbd
```

Section labels should be:

* Small
* Muted
* Uppercase or subtle typography
* Visually separated from navigation items

Do not over-group.

A section should contain enough related items to justify the heading.

layout.title: Navigation Item Rules
layout.content:
Navigation items (hand-built from Button's ghost/link variant — there is no dedicated Navigation component) should have:

* Clear label
* Optional icon
* Strong hover state
* Obvious active state
* Comfortable click target

Recommended hierarchy:

```text
Inactive:
muted foreground

Hover:
subtle background

Active:
primary-tinted background
primary/strong foreground
```

Avoid making every item look like a Button.

Navigation should visually feel different from action controls.

layout.title: Container
layout.content:
Use `Container` to control readable page width.

Prefer:

```text
Full viewport
 └── Container
      └── Content
```

Do not allow text-heavy interfaces to become excessively wide.

For documentation:

* Keep reading width comfortable.
* Allow code examples to use more horizontal space.
* Keep navigation independent from the reading column.

layout.title: Divider
layout.content:
Use `Divider` only when whitespace is insufficient to communicate separation.

Prefer:

```text
Section

large spacing

Next Section
```

over:

```text
Section
────────────
Next Section
```

Use Dividers primarily for:

* Navigation groups
* Dense settings
* Table-like layouts
* Clearly separated sections

Do not place Dividers everywhere.

layout.title: Responsive Design
layout.content:
Design mobile-first.

Desktop:

```text
Sidebar + Main Content
```

Tablet:

```text
Collapsed Sidebar + Main Content
```

Mobile:

```text
Top Bar
Content
```

Navigation should become more compact rather than simply shrinking.

Forms should become single-column where necessary.

Cards should stack naturally.

Tables may require:

* horizontal scrolling
* responsive transformation
* reduced columns

Never allow the layout to become horizontally broken.

See the Breakpoint Checklist (section 59) for the widths and checks every page must pass.

layout.title: Spacing Rules
layout.content:
Use spacing to establish hierarchy.

Use smaller spacing:

* Within a component
* Between label and input
* Between icon and text

Use larger spacing:

* Between sections
* Between page regions
* Before major headings

Avoid equal spacing everywhere.

Unequal spacing creates hierarchy.

layout.title: Color Rules
layout.content:
Use color semantically.

Primary color:

* Primary actions
* Active navigation
* Important interactive elements
* Focus states

Text colors:

* `text-foreground` for headings and titles
* `text-secondary` for paragraphs and supporting text
* `text-muted-foreground` for metadata and hints

Semantic colors:

* Success
* Warning
* Error
* Info

Do not use many unrelated accent colors.

A modern interface should generally have:

```text
1 primary brand color
+
neutral system
+
semantic colors
```

layout.title: Border Rules
layout.content:
Borders should clarify structure, not decorate it.

Prefer:

```text
spacing
+
subtle background differences
```

before adding borders.

Use borders for:

* Inputs
* Tables
* Cards when necessary
* Dividers
* Clear interactive boundaries

Avoid heavy borders around every element.

layout.title: Radius Rules
layout.content:
Use consistent corner radii.

Do not randomly mix:

```text
rounded-sm
rounded-md
rounded-lg
rounded-xl
rounded-full
```

Use full rounding primarily for:

* Chips
* Badges
* Avatars
* Compact controls

Use moderate rounding for:

* Cards
* Inputs
* Buttons
* Modals

layout.title: Type Scale
layout.content:
Use one fixed, responsive type scale on every page:

```text
Display / H1  text-4xl sm:text-5xl lg:text-6xl font-bold tracking-tight
H2            text-3xl sm:text-4xl font-semibold tracking-tight
H3            text-xl sm:text-2xl font-semibold
Body          text-base
Small         text-sm
Meta          text-xs
```

Rules:

* Never use more than 4 text sizes on one screen.
* Add `text-balance` to headings so lines break evenly.
* Add `text-pretty` to paragraphs to avoid single-word last lines.
* Step headings down one level at a time. Do not jump from H1 straight to small text.
* `tracking-tight` only on `text-3xl` and larger. Everything smaller stays at the default tracking.
* Line-height comes from the text-size class. Do not add `leading-*` on top of it.

layout.title: Readable Measure
layout.content:
Long lines are hard to read.

* Paragraphs: `max-w-prose` or `max-w-2xl`.
* Headings may run wider: `max-w-3xl`.
* Never let body text stretch the full width of a wide container.

The layout can be wide. The reading column should not be.

layout.title: Spacing Rhythm
layout.content:
Use the 4/8 spacing scale only. Space shrinks as you go deeper into the layout.

```text
Page gutters        px-4 sm:px-6 lg:px-8
Between sections    py-16 sm:py-20 lg:py-28
Between blocks      mt-10 / mt-12
Heading to body     mt-4
Inside a component  gap-2 / gap-3
```

Big gaps separate ideas. Small gaps group them. If everything has the same gap, nothing is grouped.

layout.title: Grid & Layout Patterns
layout.content:
Build layouts from a few reliable patterns:

* **Card grid:** `grid grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3 gap-4 sm:gap-6`.
* **Split:** text and visual side by side with `lg:grid-cols-2`, alternating sides from one section to the next.
* **Bento:** one large tile (`lg:col-span-2`) with smaller tiles around it, instead of identical boxes.
* **Asymmetric:** `lg:grid-cols-[2fr_1fr]` for main content plus a side column. Grid templates like this are the one allowed exception to the no-arbitrary-values rule.

Add `min-w-0` to flex and grid children that contain text, so truncation works instead of overflowing.

Avoid the default "three equal cards in a row" on every section.

layout.title: Hero / Above the Fold
layout.content:
The hero must answer "what is this and why should I care" within 5 seconds.

Recommended order:

```text
Badge            short eyebrow (New, Beta, v2.0)
H1               value proposition, under 10 words
Lead text        text-lg text-secondary, one or two sentences
Actions          one primary Button + one secondary Button
Proof            real product screenshot, stat row, or customer logos
```

* Left-align by default. Center only short, single-message heroes.
* Use a split layout (text left, visual right) on `lg` and stack on mobile.
* One primary action only. The second action is outline or ghost.

layout.title: Focal Point & Visual Interest
layout.content:
Eye-catching does not mean piling on effects. Shadows on content surfaces stay banned. Gradients, glows and blur are allowed only as brand effects: theme tokens only, one effect per element.

Visual interest comes from:

* **Scale contrast:** a very large headline next to small, quiet metadata.
* **One bold element per viewport:** a single `bg-primary` block, button or highlight that the eye lands on first.
* **Surface layering:** alternate sections between `bg-background`, `bg-card` and `bg-accent` bands to create depth without shadows.
* **Big numbers:** metrics in large type with `tabular-nums`.
* **Real imagery:** product screenshots and photos, not decorative filler.
* **One brand accent:** gradient headline words, a soft primary glow or a theme-colored animated background, never all of them on one screen.
* **Whitespace:** give the most important element more space than anything around it.

Color ratio: roughly 60% neutral surfaces, 30% text and borders, 10% primary.

layout.title: Section Variety
layout.content:
A page should feel composed, not stamped out.

* Never use the same layout for two sections in a row.
* Mix patterns: split, card grid, bento, full-width band, stat row, testimonial, FAQ, CTA band.
* Alternate background surfaces between neighbouring sections.
* End every landing page with a clear call-to-action section.

layout.title: Breakpoint Checklist
layout.content:
Design mobile-first, then check every page at:

```text
360px   small phone
768px   tablet
1024px  small laptop
1280px  desktop
1536px  large desktop
```

At every width:

* No horizontal scroll.
* Touch targets are at least 44px.
* Navigation collapses into a Drawer below `md`.
* Tables sit inside `overflow-x-auto`.
* Images use an `aspect-*` class with `object-cover`, so nothing shifts while loading.
* On mobile, stack content in order of importance (use `order-*` when the source order differs).

components.title: Cards
components.content:
Use `Card` when content represents a meaningful visual group.

Good:

```text
Card
 ├── CardHeader (optional)
 ├── CardBody (compulsory whenever there's body content)
 └── CardFooter (optional)
```

`Card` itself renders no padding — it's just the border/background/radius shell. All spacing lives in `CardHeader`/`CardBody`/`CardFooter`. Content placed directly inside `<Card>` without `<CardBody>` renders flush against the border with no padding and visibly breaks the layout, so once you've decided to use Card, wrapping its body content in `<CardBody>` is not optional the way `CardHeader`/`CardFooter` are.

Use Cards for:

* Dashboard statistics
* Settings groups
* Product previews
* Related information
* Independent content blocks

Do NOT wrap everything in Cards.

Avoid:

```text
Page
 └── Card
      └── Card
           └── Card
```

Nested cards should be rare.

If content is already visually grouped by whitespace, a Card may not be necessary.

components.title: Typography
components.content:
Typography should create hierarchy without requiring excessive decoration.

Recommended hierarchy:

```text
Page title
↓
Section title
↓
Component title
↓
Body text
↓
Metadata
```

Use:

* Strong weight for headings
* Regular weight for descriptions
* `text-secondary` for paragraphs and descriptions
* Muted color for metadata
* Comfortable line-height for reading — but from the text-size class itself (text-sm, text-base, text-lg, ...), not a separate leading-* utility layered on top; the text-size class already pairs a line-height, so adding leading-* alongside it is redundant

See Type Scale (section 52) and Readable Measure (section 53) for exact classes.

Avoid:

* Excessive bold text
* Too many font sizes
* All-caps body text
* Huge headings on every page
* Centering everything
* Adding leading-* on top of a text-size class that already sets line-height

components.title: Badge
components.content:
Use `Badge` for compact semantic information.

Good:

```text
v1.0
New
Beta
Active
Deprecated
Success
Warning
```

Bad:

```text
Every navigation item
Every card
Every paragraph
Every heading
```

A Badge should communicate information, not decoration.

components.title: Chip
components.content:
Use `Chip` for lightweight categories or selectable labels.

Good:

```text
React
Tailwind
TypeScript
Frontend
Design
```

Use Chip when users may perceive the value as a category, filter, or tag.

Do not use Badge and Chip interchangeably.

components.title: Button
components.content:
Buttons represent actions.

Hierarchy:

```text
Primary Button
Secondary Button
Tertiary / subtle Button
Destructive Button
```

Every page should generally have one visually dominant primary action, when an important action exists.

Avoid having multiple primary buttons competing with each other.

Example:

```text
Create Project        ← Primary

Import        Export  ← Secondary
```

components.title: Icon Button
components.content:
Use `Icon Button` when the action is universally understandable from the icon or when space is limited.

Good examples:

* Close
* Search
* Settings
* More
* Edit
* Delete
* Copy
* Previous
* Next

Use `Tooltip` when an icon's meaning is not immediately obvious.

Never sacrifice usability for minimalism.

components.title: Input / Form Components
components.content:
Forms should feel calm and structured.

Recommended:

```text
Form Section
 ├── Label
 ├── Input
 ├── Description
 └── Error
```

Group related fields.

Do not place every field in a separate Card.

Use:

* Input for text
* Textarea for long text
* Select for predefined options
* Checkbox for independent choices
* RadioGroup for mutually exclusive choices
* Switch for immediate on/off settings
* Slider for ranges
* Number Input for numeric values
* Date Picker for dates
* Time Picker for times
* File Upload for files

Placeholders, compulsory:

* Every Input, Textarea, Select, Number Input, Date Picker, Time Picker and search field must have a `placeholder`.
* The placeholder shows an example or format of the expected value: "you@company.com", "Search projects...", "e.g. Q3 marketing plan".
* A placeholder is a hint, never a replacement for the Label. Keep the visible Label and add the placeholder.
* Keep placeholders short and in sentence case. Do not repeat the label word for word ("Email" label → "you@company.com", not "Email").

components.title: Modal
components.content:
Use Modal for focused decisions or short tasks.

Good:

* Confirm deletion
* Create item
* Edit item
* Important settings
* Focused forms

Do not use Modal for:

* Long documentation
* Large dashboards
* Complex workflows
* Information that deserves its own page

If the content requires significant scrolling, consider a page or Drawer instead.

Modal overflow, compulsory:

* A Modal must never grow taller than the viewport. Cap the modal body height (for example `max-h-[70vh]` or `max-h-[calc(100vh-8rem)]`) and give the body `overflow-y-auto`.
* Only the body scrolls. Keep the header (title, close button) and footer (actions) fixed and always visible.
* Never let content be clipped or push the action buttons off screen. If the content can exceed the available height (long forms, lists, terms, previews), apply the vertical scroll.
* Do not add horizontal scroll to a Modal. Wrap or reflow wide content instead.

components.title: Drawer
components.content:
Use Drawer for contextual content that should remain connected to the current page.

Good:

* Filters
* Detail views
* Editing
* Mobile navigation
* Secondary settings

Drawer is especially useful when the user should keep the underlying page context.

components.title: Dropdown
components.content:
Use Dropdown for actions or compact menus.

Good:

```text
More
 ├── Edit
 ├── Duplicate
 ├── Archive
 └── Delete
```

Do not use Dropdown when users need to compare multiple persistent options.

Use Select instead for form selection.

components.title: Tooltip
components.content:
Use Tooltip for clarification, not essential information.

Good:

```text
Icon Button
    ↓
Tooltip: "Copy"
```

Do not hide essential instructions inside tooltips.

components.title: Popover
components.content:
Use Popover for contextual controls or additional information without leaving the page.

Good:

* Advanced filters
* Color selection
* Small configuration panels
* Additional metadata
* Contextual actions

Popover content should remain lightweight.

components.title: Tabs
components.content:
Use Tabs when multiple related views share the same context.

Good:

```text
Overview | Activity | Settings
```

Do not use Tabs simply because the page has multiple sections.

If users should see the sections together, use normal page sections.

components.title: Table
components.content:
Use Table when users need to compare structured records.

Good:

* Users
* Orders
* Transactions
* Logs
* Products

Provide:

* Clear column hierarchy
* Adequate spacing
* Row hover where useful
* Pagination when necessary
* Empty state
* Loading state

Avoid overly dense tables unless the product specifically requires high information density.

components.title: List
components.content:
Use List when records are naturally read vertically.

Good:

* Notifications
* Tasks
* Activities
* Messages
* Search results

Prefer List over Table when users don't need column-based comparison.

components.title: Empty State
components.content:
Empty states should explain:

1. What is empty?
2. Why it matters?
3. What should the user do next?

Example:

```text
No projects yet

Create your first project to start organizing your work.

[ Create Project ]
```

Do not create empty states that only say:

> No data found.

components.title: Alert / Callout
components.content:
Use `Callout` for persistent contextual information inside the page.

Use it for:

* Important information
* Warnings
* Success states
* Errors
* Notices
* System status
* Migration messages

Example:

```text
[Warning]

Your storage is almost full.
Consider removing unused files.
```

Use `Callout` when the message belongs to the page's content flow.

Do not use Callout for every notification.

For temporary notifications, use the toast system.

Callout hierarchy:

```text
Error
Warning
Success
Info
Neutral
```

Use semantic types correctly.

components.title: Progress
components.content:
Use Progress when users need to understand completion.

Good:

* Upload progress
* Onboarding
* Course completion
* Project progress
* Storage usage

Do not use progress bars decoratively.

Progress should represent measurable progress.

components.title: Skeleton
components.content:
Use Skeleton when content is loading and the final layout is known.

The skeleton should resemble the final content structure.

Avoid replacing the entire page with a generic spinner when the layout can be preserved.

components.title: Spinner
components.content:
Use Spinner for short, localized loading operations.

Good:

```text
[Save] → spinner → Saving...
```

Avoid full-page spinners for normal page loading when Skeleton can preserve layout.

components.title: Accordion
components.content:
Use Accordion when information is optional or secondary.

Good:

* FAQs
* Advanced settings
* Documentation sections
* Additional details

Do not hide primary information inside Accordions.

components.title: Breadcrumb
components.content:
Use Breadcrumb when the page has meaningful hierarchy.

Example:

```text
Documentation / Components / Forms / Input
```

Do not use Breadcrumb on simple pages where there is no useful hierarchy.

components.title: Pagination
components.content:
Use Pagination when users need to navigate large datasets.

Use it with:

* Tables
* Search results
* Large lists

Do not paginate small datasets unnecessarily.

components.title: Stepper
components.content:
Use Stepper for multi-step processes.

Example:

```text
Account → Details → Review → Complete
```

Each step should have a meaningful stage.

Do not use Stepper for ordinary navigation.

components.title: Image / Avatar
components.content:
Images should support content.

Use:

* Image for visual content
* Avatar for people
* Avatar Group for teams/participants

Do not add decorative images simply to fill empty space.

components.title: Carousel
components.content:
Use Carousel only when multiple visual/content items benefit from horizontal browsing.

Good:

* Product screenshots
* Testimonials
* Image galleries
* Featured content

Do not use Carousel for content that users need to compare simultaneously.

components.title: Shadows
components.content:
Never add a shadow yourself, compulsory. Prefer:

```text
background
+
border
+
spacing
```

over a shadow on anything you're styling by hand — buttons, cards, inputs, hand-built panels.

This is about classNames/markup you author. A number of `@neuctra/ui` components ship their own built-in elevation shadow as part of their default design (overlay/floating components like Modal, Dropdown, Popover, Drawer, Tooltip, and others like Table, DatePicker's calendar panel, Avatar's status dot, Kbd, and the Toast notification, among others — this isn't an exhaustive list to memorize). Leave every component's shipped defaults exactly as they ship: never add a shadow yourself, and never strip a component's built-in one with an override either — both are the same mistake in opposite directions.

components.title: Documentation UI Rules
components.content:
For component documentation, prefer:

```text
Sidebar
+
Documentation Container
+
Breadcrumb / Section Context
+
Component Title
+
Description
+
Live Preview
+
Code
+
Usage Guidelines
+
Props
+
Accessibility
+
FAQ
```

The documentation page should prioritize the component preview and developer understanding.

Keep code visually distinct from prose.

components.title: Component Preview Rules
components.content:
Every preview should feel like a real product interface.

Do not make previews look like isolated component experiments.

Instead of:

```text
Button
Button
Button
```

prefer contextual examples:

```text
Project Settings

Project name
[ My Project                  ]

[ Cancel ] [ Save Changes ]
```

This demonstrates how the component actually behaves in a product.

components.title: Do Not Overwrite Built-in Component Design
components.content:
Use each `@neuctra/ui` component's built-in design — its default spacing, radius, colors, and layout — as-is.

Do not pass a `className` just to restyle a component's built-in appearance because of personal preference. The component's own design is already the intended, consistent look.

Only override with Tailwind's `!` important-modifier (e.g. `!bg-red-500`, `!p-2`, `!rounded-lg`) when there is a real, specific need:

* The component's default would otherwise break the current page's existing layout.
* The default collides or conflicts with the current UI/design of the site.
* The component has no prop for the needed variation, and leaving the default would visually damage the surrounding design.

Never reach for `!important` overrides as a routine styling habit, a stylistic preference, or 'just because'.

Prefer:

> built-in component design → prop-based variation (variant, size, etc.) → `!important` override (rare, only to prevent breakage)

over:

> restyle every component by default with className overrides

A component that has been overridden with `!important` on every use is a sign the component itself, or the way it's being used, is wrong — not that every instance needs forcing.

components.title: Paragraph Text Color
components.content:
Use `text-secondary` for all paragraph text: body copy, section descriptions, card descriptions, and supporting text under headings.

Do not use `text-muted-foreground` for paragraphs. It is too low-contrast for reading text.

Keep `text-muted-foreground` for small, low-priority text only:

* Timestamps
* Metadata
* Captions
* Placeholders
* Helper and hint text
* Disabled states

Use `text-foreground` for headings, titles, and anything that needs full emphasis.

`secondary` is a text color only. Do not use it as a background (`bg-secondary`).

Order of emphasis:

```text
text-foreground        ← headings
↓
text-secondary         ← paragraphs
↓
text-muted-foreground  ← metadata and hints
```

Token values:

* Light theme: `--secondary: #3f3f46`
* Dark theme: `--secondary: #d4d4d8`

components.title: Code Blocks
components.content:
Whenever the UI shows a code block (snippets, install commands, API examples, config files, documentation), use the `react-syntax-highlighter` package (`"react-syntax-highlighter": "^15.6.6"`). Never hand-roll a code block with a plain `<pre>` and manual coloring, and never use another highlighting library.

Install:

```bash
npm install react-syntax-highlighter@^15.6.6
```

Usage:

```jsx
import { Prism as SyntaxHighlighter } from "react-syntax-highlighter";
import { oneDark } from "react-syntax-highlighter/dist/esm/styles/prism";

<SyntaxHighlighter
  language="tsx"
  style={oneDark}
  showLineNumbers={false}
  wrapLongLines={false}
  customStyle={{ margin: 0, borderRadius: "0.75rem", fontSize: "0.875rem" }}
>
  {code}
</SyntaxHighlighter>
```

Rules:

* Use the Prism build and always set the correct `language`.
* The highlighter's syntax theme is the only allowed exception to the theme-tokens-only color rule. Everything around it (wrapper, header, copy button, filename) uses Neuctra UI tokens and components.
* Give multi-line blocks a small header with the filename or language and a copy button.
* Long lines scroll horizontally inside the block (`overflow-x-auto`); the block must never widen the page.
* Inline code in a sentence stays a styled `<code>` element, not the highlighter.

components.title: Dashboard Charts
components.content:
When you build a dashboard (analytics, admin, CRM, reports, any page that shows stats over time or comparisons), visualize the stats with ApexCharts using `apexcharts` + `react-apexcharts`. Do not use another chart library and do not fake charts with divs or static images.

Install:

```bash
npm install apexcharts react-apexcharts
```

Usage (Next.js: load the chart client-side only):

```jsx
"use client";
import dynamic from "next/dynamic";
const Chart = dynamic(() => import("react-apexcharts"), { ssr: false });

const css = (name) =>
  getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue(name).trim();

const options = {
  chart: { toolbar: { show: false }, fontFamily: "inherit", background: "transparent" },
  colors: [css("--primary"), css("--info"), css("--warning")],
  grid: { borderColor: css("--border"), strokeDashArray: 4 },
  xaxis: { categories, labels: { style: { colors: css("--muted-foreground") } } },
  yaxis: { labels: { style: { colors: css("--muted-foreground") } } },
  tooltip: { theme: isDark ? "dark" : "light" },
  dataLabels: { enabled: false },
  stroke: { curve: "smooth", width: 2 },
};

<Chart type="area" height={300} options={options} series={series} />
```

Rules:

* Chart colors come from the theme CSS variables (read with getComputedStyle), never hardcoded hex values. Re-read them when the theme switches between light and dark.
* Place each chart inside a Card with a CardHeader (title, short description, optional range selector) and the chart in CardBody.
* Pick the chart by the question: line/area for trends over time, bar for comparing categories, donut/radial only for a few parts of a whole (max 5 slices), sparkline inside stat tiles.
* Keep KPI stat tiles as numbers first; add a chart only where a trend or comparison helps.
* Hide the toolbar, disable data labels on dense series, keep the grid subtle, and set an explicit height so the layout does not jump while loading.
* Charts must be responsive: use `width="100%"` and stack chart cards to a single column on small screens.

accessibilityInteraction.title: Accessibility
accessibilityInteraction.content:
Accessibility is part of the design.

Always consider:

* Keyboard navigation
* Focus states
* Screen readers
* Color contrast
* Semantic HTML
* Clear labels
* Button names
* Input descriptions
* Error messages
* Touch target sizes

Never communicate meaning using color alone.

accessibilityInteraction.title: Interaction Design
accessibilityInteraction.content:
Every interactive element should provide feedback.

Examples:

```text
Default
→ Hover
→ Active
→ Focus
→ Disabled
→ Loading
→ Success/Error
```

Do not animate everything.

Use subtle transitions for:

* Hover
* Opening/closing
* State changes
* Navigation
* Feedback

Motion should explain interaction, not distract.

modernDesign.title: Imagery & Media
modernDesign.content:
* Use consistent aspect ratios: `aspect-video`, `aspect-square`, or `aspect-[4/3]` (allowed ratio).
* Use one corner radius for all images on a page.
* Always write real, descriptive `alt` text.
* Lazy-load images below the fold.
* Prefer real product screenshots over stock illustrations or abstract shapes.

modernDesign.title: Iconography
modernDesign.content:
* Use lucide-react icons only.
* Match icon size to the text beside it: 16px with `text-sm`, 20px with `text-base`, 24px next to headings.
* Keep the same stroke width across the whole interface.
* Icons support labels. They do not replace them, except in an IconButton with a Tooltip.
* Do not wrap every icon in a colored circle.

modernDesign.title: Motion (Framer Motion)
modernDesign.content:
Motion explains a change and adds a light brand feel. Aim for a medium level: noticeable, never busy.

Use Framer Motion for page and section motion. It already ships as a dependency of `@neuctra/ui`:

```tsx
import { motion, MotionConfig } from "framer-motion";
```

```text
Hover / press       transition-colors duration-150, lift y -2 to -4px, press scale 0.97
Open / close        200 to 300ms, ease-out
Section reveal      opacity 0 to 1, y 16 to 0, 0.4 to 0.6s, ease-out, once
Grid / list stagger 0.06 to 0.1s between items, at most about 6 items
Hero on load        one short reveal (under 0.6s), nothing else animates on load
Background loops    slow (8s or more), low opacity, one per viewport
```

* Wrap the page in `<MotionConfig reducedMotion="user">`.
* Reveal with `whileInView` and `viewport={{ once: true, amount: 0.2 }}`. Never re-animate on every scroll.
* Animate only opacity and transform (x, y, scale). Never animate width, height, top, left or the layout of text being read.
* Use `ease-out` tweens or soft springs (`stiffness` about 200 to 300, `damping` 25 or more). No bounce, wobble, scale-105 zooms, parallax on text, or infinite loops on content.
* Animate sections and grid items, not every element. Wrap `@neuctra/ui` components in a `motion.div`; do not restyle their internal animation.
* Marketing and public pages: section reveals, stagger and an optional animated background. App and dashboard pages: hover/press, open/close and list item enter/exit only.

modernDesign.title: Microcopy
modernDesign.content:
Words are part of the design.

* Sentence case for headings, buttons and labels.
* Buttons start with a verb: "Create project", not "Submit".
* Headlines state the benefit, not the feature name.
* One idea per sentence. Short sentences.
* No em dashes. Use a period, comma or colon instead.

antiAiDesignRules.title: Avoid AI-Generated UI Patterns
antiAiDesignRules.content:
Never generate:

* Multicolor or rainbow gradients, or any color outside the theme
* Shadows on buttons or cards, or large stacked shadows (shadow-xl, shadow-2xl)
* A gradient on every heading, or gradient buttons
* More than one animated background per viewport
* Glow on buttons or text
* Excessive rounded containers, every section inside a Card
* Random decorative icons, unnecessary badges, emoji as icons
* Multiple primary buttons, huge empty spaces, decorative statistics without meaning
* Repeated identical layouts

Allowed when on brand: theme-colored gradient headline words, soft primary glows, frosted sticky bars, and a theme-colored animated background that respects reduced motion.

goldenRule.title: Golden Rule
goldenRule.content:
Do not ask:

> "Which components can I put on this page?"

Ask:

> "What does the user need to understand and do, and which Neuctra UI component communicates that most naturally?"

The best Neuctra UI interface is not the one that uses the most components.

It is the one where **every component has a purpose.**

motion.install: framer-motion ships as a dependency of @neuctra/ui. If the project does not resolve it, run: npm install framer-motion
motion.level: medium: visible section reveals and small interaction feedback, never busy

presets.sectionReveal: <motion.section initial={{ opacity: 0, y: 16 }} whileInView={{ opacity: 1, y: 0 }} viewport={{ once: true, amount: 0.2 }} transition={{ duration: 0.5, ease: "easeOut" }}>
presets.hoverLift: <motion.div whileHover={{ y: -3 }} whileTap={{ scale: 0.97 }} transition={{ type: "spring", stiffness: 260, damping: 26 }}>
presets.animatedBackground: <motion.div aria-hidden className="pointer-events-none absolute -z-10 left-1/2 top-0 size-96 -translate-x-1/2 rounded-full bg-primary/20 blur-[120px]" animate={{ opacity: [0.5, 0.8, 0.5], scale: [1, 1.1, 1] }} transition={{ duration: 10, repeat: Infinity, ease: "easeInOut" }} />

byPageKind.marketing: Hero reveal on load, section reveals on scroll, staggered feature and pricing grids, at most one animated background per viewport.
byPageKind.app: Hover/press feedback, open/close and list item enter/exit (AnimatePresence) only. No scroll reveals or animated backgrounds on dashboards, settings or data pages.
